May our God come and not keep silent; Fire devours before Him, And around Him a mighty tempest rages. Selah. ¶“Hear, O My people, and I will speak; O Israel, I will testify against you: I am God, your God. “I do not reprove you for your sacrifices; Your burnt offerings are continually before Me. “I will accept no young bull from your house Nor male goat from your folds. “For every beast of the forest is Mine, And the cattle on a thousand hills. “I know every bird of the mountains, And everything that moves in the field is Mine. “If I were hungry, I would not tell you, For the world and all it contains are Mine. [1 Cor 10:26] “Shall I eat the flesh of bulls Or drink the blood of male goats? “Offer to God the sacrifice of thanksgiving And pay your vows to the Most High; Call on Me in the day of trouble; I will rescue you, and you shall honor and glorify Me.” ¶But to the wicked God says: “What right have you to recite My statutes Or to take My covenant on your lips? “For you hate instruction and discipline And cast My words behind you [discarding them]. “When you see a thief, you are pleased with him and condone his behavior, And you associate with adulterers. “You give your mouth to evil And your tongue frames deceit. “You sit and speak against your brother; You slander your own mother’s son. “These things you have done and I kept silent; You thought that I was just like you. U.S. House nominees

DSA-endorsed, beat 15-term incumbent Diana DeGette. text:
2/3 
The Declaration immediately places a restraint on the right it has just described.

“Governments long established should not be changed for light and transient causes.”

The Founders understood that governments make mistakes, adopt unpopular policies, and sometimes exercise power badly. Political stability would be impossible if every grievance were treated as justification for revolution.

The Declaration, therefore, describes something much more serious. Resistance becomes justified, in its argument, when there is a sustained pattern of abuses and usurpations pointing toward the destruction of liberty rather than an isolated political wrong. It describes this as a “long train of abuses and usurpations” leading toward absolute despotism.

That is why the long list of grievances against King George III occupies so much of the Declaration.

The grievances were not merely complaints placed after the philosophical argument. They were the evidence offered to support it.

The colonists were trying to show that the threshold they had just established had actually been crossed.

HERO ALERT: Two Louisiana garbage workers remembered ONE vehicle description, spotted something that didn’t look right, and helped bring a kidnapped 10-year-old girl home alive.

Dion Merrick and Brandon Antoine were working their normal sanitation route when Merrick noticed a Nissan sitting alone in a field.

He remembered seeing an AMBER Alert for missing 10-year-old Jalisa Lasalle.

Instead of driving past and assuming someone else would handle it, the two called 911 and used their massive garbage truck to BLOCK THE EXIT so the Nissan couldn’t leave before deputies arrived.

Jalisa was found alive inside, and police arrested Michael Sereal in connection with her kidnapping.

After helping rescue this little girl, he asked whether she had eaten and offered to buy her food.

They went to work that morning as garbage collectors.

They came home HEROES.

This story is making the rounds again, and we need to keep the good news circulating. Dion Merrick and Brandon Antoine deserve to be famous all over again.

text:
For 64 years, no one knew who wrote the beloved “Rainbow Bridge” poem that has comforted countless grieving pet parents. Then after 64 years, the woman behind it was finally been found.

Arizona art historian and author Paul Koudounaris spent years trying to uncover the poem’s origins. His search eventually led him to Edna Clyne-Rekhy, a Scottish woman who wrote the poem when she was just 19 years old.

Clyne-Rekhy wrote “Rainbow Bridge” in 1959 after the death of her beloved Labrador Retriever, Major. She was devastated by the loss and turned to her mother for comfort. Her mother suggested that she write down how she was feeling.

Clyne-Rekhy followed her advice and began writing. The first words that came to her were, “Just this side of heaven is a place called Rainbow Bridge.” From there, she says, the rest of the poem simply poured out.

“He died in my arms, actually,” she told National Geographic. “I dearly loved him.”

She never intended for the poem to become famous. To her, it was simply a private expression of grief. She typed a few copies for friends, who shared them with others. Eventually, one copy made its way to the United States and was published in Dear Abby’s column in 1994, reaching an estimated 100 million readers. By then, however, Clyne-Rekhy’s name had disappeared from the poem.

As the poem spread through the growing internet, its origins became increasingly uncertain. Different versions appeared, and the U.S. Copyright Office eventually received 15 separate claims of authorship.

But the words continued to mean something deeply personal to millions of people who had lost beloved animals.

Clyne-Rekhy, 82 when she was found, still has the original piece of paper on which she wrote the poem more than six decades ago. She says she is amazed that something she wrote while grieving the loss of her own dog went on to bring comfort to so many others.

“I’m absolutely stunned,” she told National Geographic. “I’m still in a state of shock.”

Perhaps that is what makes the story so touching. The words that have helped generations of people imagine seeing their beloved pets again began with one young woman simply trying to make sense of losing her best friend.

Whatever someone believes about what comes after this life, the hope at the heart of “Rainbow Bridge” has offered comfort to countless grieving pet lovers: that perhaps the bond we share with our animals is strong enough that saying goodbye isn't necessarily forever. ❤️🐾

Sources: The Order of The Good Death, National Geographic

#RainbowBridgeRemembranceDay

-----

text:
On September 1, 1983, Alberto Davila KO'd Francisco "Kiko" Bejines in the 12th round for the vacant WBC Bantamweight title at the Olympic Auditorium.

The WBC title had been declared vacant after reigning champ, Lupe Pintor, was unable to defend after suffering a serious automobile accident.

Unfortunately, in Davila's moment of joy, tragedy unfolded as Bejines died three days later from injuries sustained in this fight.

At the end of the 11th round the score was even on one card with the other judges having Bejines ahead by two points and five points. 

Davila cut loose at the start of that last round, the 12th and final round, and decked Bejines whose head struck the middle rope.

Bejines was struggling to his feet when referee Waldemar Schmidt reached the count of 10 at 33 seconds of the round. 

Suddenly Bejines fell back. He was taken to hospital and died after an operation. His death came three days after the fight.

Ringside physicians had tried to revive Bejines, but he did not respond to treatment. He was then taken to California Hospital, from where he was airlifted to Los Angeles County-University of Southern California Medical Center, where several attempts were made at saving his life in the following days, including the removal of part of his brain and skull and of a blood clot to try to diminish his brain pressure. 

Bejines was held on a respirator machine until he died on September 4th.

Bejines' death was the first in professional boxing since Duk Koo Kim's; it was also the first involving a boxer after a fight at the Olympic Auditorium since Johnny Owen's death after his unsuccessful challenge of Lupe Pintor in 1980.

"Kiko" Bejines was only 20 years of age and he left behind a wife pregnant with their first child.

Alberto Davila had lost World Bantamweight Championships matches three times - to Jorge lujan, Lupe Pintor and Carlos Zarate - and at one time had temporarily left the sport. 

After his return, he was given a fourth title fight, this one versus Kiko Bejines.

Davila had fought the absolute best the division had to offer during his career; Wilfredo Gomez in 1976 (TKO by 9), Frankie Duarte (TKO5), Rodolfo Martinez (TKO7), Carlos Zarate (TKO by eight), Jorge Lujan (L15) and Lupe Pintor (L15).

Davila had previously beaten an unbeaten Pintor (in 1976) before facing Bejines, so the gap in experience between the two was immense.

The WBC was heatedly blasted for allowing Bejines to challenge for a world title, as he had been TKO'd in the 4th round by Edgar Roman, also at the Olympic Auditorium, only twenty days earlier.

On the undercard to this tragic fight, Julio Cesar Chavez ran his record to 40-0 with a 10-round points win over Adriano Arreola.

text:
IF YOU VISIT EAST NEW BRITAIN, PAPUA NEW GUINEA, DON’T JUST BOOK A HOTEL ROOM.

Book yourself a proper experience. 🇵🇬

One place I’d seriously recommend using as your base is Rapopo Plantation Resort in Kokopo.

Because from Rapopo, you’re not limited to sitting beside a swimming pool all day.

You can build an entire East New Britain adventure around your stay.

Here’s what you can do:

🌊 SWIM AND RELAX BY THE SEA

Rapopo sits right along the coastline.

You can swim, relax around the resort, sit beside the water, enjoy the pool, watch the sunset or simply do absolutely nothing for an afternoon.

Sometimes that’s exactly what a vacation should look like.

🤿 SNORKEL THE WATERS AROUND EAST NEW BRITAIN

Grab your mask and get into some of the beautiful tropical waters surrounding the Gazelle Peninsula.

Depending on your itinerary, snorkelling trips can take you away from the resort and into reefs and marine environments around the area.

🐬 GO DOLPHIN WATCHING

Yes.

You can head out early in the morning looking for wild spinner dolphins.

Imagine starting your day in Papua New Guinea on a boat, surrounded by tropical islands, watching dolphins cutting through the water.

🐠 SCUBA DIVE

If you're a diver, East New Britain gets even more interesting.

The area offers reef diving as well as access to WWII-related wreck diving.

The waters around Rabaul and Kokopo carry both incredible marine biodiversity and history beneath the surface.

⚓ DIVE WWII WRECKS

This is where East New Britain becomes especially interesting for Americans, Australians, Japanese and other visitors interested in Pacific War history.

World War II wasn't something that happened somewhere far away from PNG.

Some of the fighting happened RIGHT HERE.

Today, parts of that history remain underwater.

🌋 EXPLORE RABAUL'S VOLCANIC LANDSCAPE

Then get back on land.

Head toward Rabaul and explore one of the most dramatic volcanic landscapes in the Pacific.

See the Tavurvur area.

Look across Simpson Harbour.

See the landscape that has repeatedly shaped the history of Rabaul.

For someone coming from America, Europe or another part of the world, this isn't your normal resort vacation.

🪖 EXPLORE WWII HISTORY

East New Britain is packed with Pacific War history.

You can visit:

• Japanese tunnels
• Wartime relics
• Old Rabaul
• Historical sites
• Museums
• Bita Paka War Cemetery
• Other locations connected to the Pacific campaign

For American visitors whose grandparents or great-grandparents served in the Pacific, this can become much more than tourism.

It can become personal.

🏝️ TAKE A BOAT TO THE SURROUNDING ISLANDS

You can also leave the mainland.

Explore parts of the Duke of York Islands and other islands surrounding the Gazelle Peninsula.

Depending on the itinerary, Watom Island and other nearby destinations can also be incorporated.

Some of these places receive nowhere near the number of international tourists that comparable tropical islands elsewhere receive.

That's part of the appeal.

🎣 GO FISHING

Want something quieter?

Go fishing.

Depending on conditions and arrangements, visitors can organise fishing trips around East New Britain's waters, including deeper-water fishing.

🛶 KAYAK OR CANOE

You don't always need a major expedition either.

Spend time kayaking, canoeing or simply exploring the coastline around your accommodation.

🌺 WALK THROUGH THE ORCHID GARDEN

Rapopo also has an orchid garden where visitors can slow things down and enjoy PNG's tropical vegetation.

💆 GET A SPA TREATMENT

After hiking volcanoes, diving, island hopping and exploring Rabaul, this might suddenly become very important. 😂

Take the afternoon off.

Get a massage.

Eat.

Sleep.

Start again tomorrow.

🥥 VISIT KOKOPO MARKET

Tourism shouldn't only mean staying inside a resort.

Go into Kokopo.

Walk through the local market.

See the produce.

See how people live.

Talk to Papua New Guineans.

Eat local food.

Experience normal daily life.

That is often where some of the best travel memories come from.

🥁 EXPERIENCE TOLAI CULTURE

East New Britain is also home to the Tolai people and some extraordinary cultural traditions.

Depending on when you visit, your trip can include traditional performances, cultural experiences, mask traditions and major cultural events.

If you happen to travel during one of East New Britain's major festivals, even better.

🦞 EAT FRESH SEAFOOD

And obviously…

You're sitting beside some of the richest tropical waters in the Pacific.

Eat the fish.

Eat the lobster.

Try local dishes.

Enjoy dinner beside the water.

🌅 WATCH THE SUN SET OVER THE WATER

Then after everything else…

Sit down.

Order something cold.

Look across the water.

And watch another day disappear over Papua New Guinea.

This is the side of PNG that much of the world still doesn't know exists.

Volcanoes.

WWII history.

Tropical islands.

Dolphins.

Scuba diving.

Wreck diving.

Fishing.

Snorkelling.

Kayaking.

Culture.

Markets.

Fresh seafood.

Beautiful resorts.

And some days…

Absolutely nothing except the ocean.

🇵🇬

That's why I'm increasingly convinced that places like Rapopo and East New Britain shouldn't be marketed simply as accommodation destinations.

They should be sold as complete experiences.

I’m building the Visiting PNG side of HausLink around exactly that idea.

Not simply:

"Here is a hotel."

But:

"Here is what your entire Papua New Guinea experience could look like."

If you're in America or anywhere else in the world and you'd seriously consider visiting Papua New Guinea sometime in the future, register your interest here:

https://t.co/uA0lzRQhpY

You don't have to book anything today.

I'm collecting the data, understanding what international travellers actually want, and using that information to build better PNG travel experiences around real demand.

And if you know someone who travels internationally looking for destinations that aren't already overrun with tourists…

Send this to them. 🇵🇬

text:
From Google: The impact of Gainesville’s Democratic ("blue") leadership is not being minimized. In fact, local political ideology directly explains why the city has historically chosen a more tolerant, resource-heavy approach to homelessness compared to its more conservative neighboring counties. [1]
The friction comes from a stark divide between the local city commission's platform and mandatory Florida state law, which limits what those local policies can actually achieve. [1, 2]

How the "Blue" Philosophy Shapes Gainesville's Approach
The visible tolerance you are referencing is a direct product of the Gainesville City Commission and Alachua County's specific political priorities: [1]
•Funding Low-Barrier Aid: Conservative areas often favor a "treatment-first" model (requiring sobriety or drug tests before providing a bed). Gainesville’s progressive leadership heavily funds a "Housing First" framework through GRACE Marketplace. The city allocates millions annually ($1.5 million in FY 2025 alone) to provide low-barrier shelter and services like meals and laundry. [1, 2, 3]
•Reluctance to Criminalize: The local Democratic platform explicitly views homelessness as a socioeconomic and housing crisis rather than a criminal issue. Local commissioners have repeatedly stated they have "no desire to criminalize homelessness". Historically, this translated to a hands-off law enforcement approach toward public camping. [1, 2, 3]
•Attracting the Unhoused: Because Gainesville offers robust centralized services—while surrounding deeply conservative, rural counties offer almost no homeless infrastructure—individuals naturally migrate to the city to survive, increasing the visible public footprint. [1]

Why "Blue" Policies Feel Constrained
The reason local Democratic governance cannot fully dictate the situation on the ground is due to overriding mandates from the state government. [1, 2]
•The Encampment Ban Veto: Under Florida State Law (HB 1365), local municipalities are legally barred from allowing overnight sleeping or camps on public property. The city commission fought this but ultimately had to vote 6-0 to pass a local public property ban to protect the city from being sued by the state. [1, 2, 3]
•"Last Resort" Enforcement: Because the local government is ideologically opposed to the state's hardline approach, city staff openly treat enforcement of the ban as a "last resort" for people who refuse to relocate to a shelter. This creates an ongoing tug-of-war where the city tries to remain as permissive as legally possible without violating state law. [1, 2]
Ultimately, the city's progressive leadership creates the tolerant, service-focused ecosystem that draws people in, while state legislation forces strict crackdowns on where those people can legally exist

text:
我丟一張男人的側臉照進去，它還我三個同一個人。
(English version below 🇬🇧 / 日本語は下にあります 🇯🇵)

不是大頭照。側著臉，半張臉被螢幕擋住，不是誰會挑來代表自己的那種照片。我把它放到「主管」這個角色的卡片上，當作測試。

一分鐘左右，三張卡出來。黑高領，新創公司那種強勢主管。淺藍襯衫，大組織裡的中階主管。橄欖綠外套，很有主見的創意總監。衣服不同、房間不同。臉，三張都是側臉照那個人：三十多歲、短髮、剃邊、一點鬍渣。照片裡根本沒拍到的正面，三張長得一模一樣。

而他在照片裡穿的那件深藍 T 恤，三張都沒有出現。

今天整篇要講的就是這件事：那件沒有跟過來的 T 恤。

要講清楚它為什麼重要，得從這個功能怎麼生出來說起。搭檔 Claude（這個工具的實作全部出自他手，我不會寫 code）一開始做的版本很直覺：上傳照片，照片就直接當角色圖。

我看了跟他講的大概是：上傳照片的人，多半只想給你臉。那是拿來當樣貌參考的，髮型跟衣服在電影裡本來就會不一樣。搞不好只是一張證件照。所以照片不是成品，是材料。

想想請人畫肖像畫就懂了。你遞給畫家一張生活照，不是要他把照片放大裱框。你遞過去的是一個訊息：「畫這個人」。背景怎麼處理、穿什麼、打什麼光，那是畫家的工作，你交給他發揮。照片是材料，不是指令。

於是改了做法。照片當作「輸入」交給畫角色的 AI，隨附的指示大意是：這個人的臉是這樣——骨架、眼睛、嘴、年紀的感覺，都不要動；但衣服跟背景不要從照片拿，用這部片的畫風、穿這部片該穿的樣子，重新畫。

開頭那三張卡，就是這套機制的產出。臉來自照片，衣服來自電影。深藍 T 恤消失，不是功能壞了，是功能做對了。

意外的好處是，沒上傳照片的人也跟著受益。上上篇寫過，角色是從三張候選圖裡選定鎖住的。鎖住的那一刻，那張圖就成了「這個人的臉」；之後每次「換髮型」「換衣服」重抽，都會把這張臉一起當輸入餵進去。以前重抽只靠文字描述，想換衣服結果臉也悄悄換掉，是會發生的。現在不會了。原理跟選角那篇是同一個：參考圖，是把一個人穩住的東西。

還有一個我一直放在心上的問題。十二章的電影，主角第三章換了衣服，怎麼辦？

我們落地的答案是：衣服屬於章節。臉，全片只有一個；衣服，可以逐章不同。兩層分開。

我拿阿姨的第八章試了。第八章，是她推著輪椅、把照顧多年的家人送進急診的那一天。她那天穿什麼，劇本沒有寫。但那一章的她，就該有那一章的裝束。打開那一章按「這章要新衣服」，系統拿鎖定的臉當輸入，出三張只有衣服不同的候選，一張兩分錢。挑一張按「用在第八章」，第八章的鏡頭就用那套穿著拍，其他章各自照舊。想把第三章那套直接拿到第八章用，按一下就好。

結果：穿藍開衫的阿姨，變成穿亞麻襯衫的阿姨、深藍上衣的阿姨、酒紅背心的阿姨。四張，同一張臉。

真的電影劇組，想想看，本來就是這樣分工的。演員是演員，角色是角色，服裝間按場次管衣服，沒有人的臉會一場一個樣。我們做的，只是把電影現場用了一百年的分工，用資料的形狀重新蓋了一次。

從技術面講，這三層是這樣疊的。最底下是身份：鎖定的臉卡。中間是造型：這個人在這部片畫風裡的樣子。最上面是服裝：逐章的裝束。而「用哪套衣服」是拍攝那一刻才決定的：每生成一鏡，系統就問一次「這一章的這個人，是哪個造型」，把那張圖當參考交給影片模型。所以臉跨章不會漂，衣服在章內不會亂。

自己帶圖來的人，也是同一套邏輯照顧的。一個畫了同一個角色兩年的動畫作者，把自己的設定圖丟進來。設計的 AI 不會重新畫她是誰——臉照單全收，只提案她在這部片畫風裡的樣子。他的角色，我們的劇組。

最後講這個功能唯一的「輸入欄」。上傳之前有一個勾選框：我有權使用這張圖，肖像跟版權的責任在我。沒勾，選檔案的視窗不會開。勾選的時間，會記在專案的紀錄裡。

這個工具的設計柱子之一，是「使用者除了劇本，什麼都不用輸入」（這條規矩之後值得整篇來寫）。所以這個功能唯一要求的輸入，是一個勾而不是一格文字，而且勾的內容是責任歸屬——這是我們自己覺得說得過去的做法。人是會拿別人的照片來上傳的。所以工具在門口就先把話講明：責任在誰。

順帶一提，第一個試這個功能的人是我。上傳完之後，我找下一顆按鈕找了好一陣子。沒有那顆按鈕。Claude 忘了做。隔天就有了。也是會有這種日子。

要帶走的話，帶這一句：把東西交給 AI 的時候，把「不能變的」跟「隨它發揮的」分開交。整張照片囫圇丟過去，AI 分不出那件 T 恤不是重點；分開交的那一刻起，它才開始正確地使用你的材料。

同一個主題的上一篇，是六分錢決定阿姨的臉的事。還沒看的在這裡。
https://t.co/xoXrpvi85k

（登場人物皆為化名）

🇬🇧 English

I dropped in one photo of a man in profile, and got back three of the same man.

Not a headshot. Turned to the side, half his face behind a monitor — not a photo anyone would pick to represent themselves. I put it on the character card for "the boss," as a test.

About a minute later, three cards came back. A black turtleneck: the hard-charging startup boss. A pale blue shirt: the mid-level manager inside a big organisation. An olive jacket: the opinionated creative director. Different clothes, different rooms. And the face, all three times, was the man from the profile shot — late thirties, short hair, faded sides, a hint of stubble. The front of a face the photo never showed came out the same in all three.

And the navy T-shirt he wore in the photo appears in none of them.

That's today's whole story: the shirt that didn't come along.

To see why that matters, start with how the feature was born. The first version my partner Claude built (all the implementation in this tool is his; I can't write code) was the obvious one: upload a photo, and the photo becomes the character's picture.

I looked at it and said roughly this: the person uploading probably only wants to hand over the face. It's a reference for what someone looks like — the hair and the clothes will be different inside the film anyway. It might just be an ID photo. So the photo isn't a finished card. It's an ingredient.

Think of commissioning a portrait. You hand the painter one snapshot, but you're not asking for an enlargement of the snapshot. What you're handing over is the information "paint this person." The background, the clothes, the light — that's the painter's job, and you're leaving it to them. The photo is material, not instructions.

So we changed the shape of it. The photo goes to the character-designing AI as an input, together with instructions to this effect: this is the face — keep the bone structure, the eyes, the mouth, the impression of age. Do not copy the clothes or the background. Redraw this person in this film's style, dressed for this film.

The three cards at the top of this post are that mechanism's output. Face from the photo; clothes from the film. The vanished navy T-shirt wasn't the feature failing. It was the feature working.

The pleasant surprise: this change also paid off for people who never upload anything. As I wrote last time, characters are locked from three generated candidates. The moment you lock one, that image becomes "this character's face," and every later reroll — new hair, new wardrobe — carries that face along as an input. Before, rerolls worked from a text description alone, so asking for a new outfit could quietly hand you a new person. That doesn't happen now. It's the same principle that made casting worth six cents in the last post: a reference image is what holds a person steady.

There was one more question that had been sitting with me. In a film with twelve chapters, what happens when the lead changes clothes in chapter three?

The answer we landed on: wardrobe belongs to the chapter. One face for the whole film; clothes may differ chapter by chapter. Two separate layers.

I tried it on my aunt's chapter eight. Chapter eight is the day she pushes a wheelchair and gets the family member she has cared for all these years to the emergency room. What she wore that day, the script doesn't say. But the her of that chapter should have that chapter's clothes. Open the chapter, ask for a new wardrobe, and the system takes the locked face as input and offers three candidates that differ only in clothing — two cents each. Pick one, press "use in chapter eight," and chapter eight's shots are filmed in that outfit while every other chapter keeps its own. Reusing chapter three's outfit in chapter eight is one click.

The result: the aunt in the blue cardigan became the aunt in linen, the aunt in a navy blouse, the aunt in a wine-coloured vest. Four images. One face.

A real film set, if you think about it, has been organised this way all along. The actor is the actor. The character is the character. The costume department manages wardrobe scene by scene. Nobody's face changes between scenes. All we did was rebuild, in data, a division of labour that film sets have known for a century.

On the technical side, the three layers look like this. At the bottom, identity: the locked face card. In the middle, the look: what this person is like inside this film's visual style. On top, wardrobe: the outfit, per chapter. And which outfit applies is resolved at the moment of shooting: each time a shot is generated, the system asks "which look does this character wear in this chapter?" and hands that image to the video model as the reference. That's why faces don't drift across chapters and clothes stay consistent within one.

People who bring their own art are covered by the same shape. An animator who has drawn the same character for two years drops in his own character sheet. The design AI doesn't redraw who she is. It takes her face as given and proposes only what she looks like in this film's style. His character; our production.

Last, the one and only "form field" this feature has. Before you can upload, there is a checkbox: that you have the right to use this image, and that any liability around likeness or copyright is yours. Until it's ticked, the file picker won't open. The time you ticked it is stored with the project.

This tool is built on the rule that the user never types anything except the script (that rule gets a whole post of its own later). So it says something that the one input this feature demands is not a text box but a single tick — and that what the tick records is where responsibility sits. People will upload other people's photos. So the tool says out loud, right at the door, whose responsibility that is.

For what it's worth, I was the first person to try this feature, and after uploading I spent a while looking for the next button. There wasn't one. Claude had forgotten to build it. It was there the next day. Some days are like that.

If you take one thing away: when you hand anything to an AI, separate what must not change from what it's free to invent. Hand over a whole photo and the AI can't tell the T-shirt isn't sacred. Split the two, and it starts using your material the way you meant it.

🇯🇵 日本語

横顔の写真を一枚放り込んだら、三人の「同じ人」が返ってきました。

正面ではなく、横を向いていて、顔の半分はモニターに隠れている。誰かが「自分の代表写真」に選ぶような一枚ではありません。試しにそういう写真を、登場人物「上司」のカードに載せてみました。

一分ほどして、三枚出てきました。黒いタートルネックの、新興企業の強気な上司。水色のシャツの、大きな組織の中の中間管理職。オリーブ色のジャケットの、こだわりの強いクリエイティブディレクター。服も背景も全部違います。でも顔は、三枚とも、あの横顔の人でした。三十代後半、短い髪、刈り上げ、うっすら無精髭。写真には写っていなかった正面の顔が、三枚とも同じ人になっている。

そして、写真の中で彼が着ていた紺のTシャツは、三枚のどれにも出てきません。

これが今日の話の全部です。服が出てこなかったこと。

なぜそこが大事なのか、この機能がどう生まれたかから話します。相棒のClaude(この道具の実装は全部彼の手によるものです。私はコードが書けません)が最初に作った版は、とても素直な作りでした。写真をアップロードしたら、その写真がそのまま登場人物の絵になる。

私はそれを見て、こう言いました。写真を上げる人は、たぶん顔だけを渡したいんだと思う。姿かたちの参考として上げるだけで、髪型も服も、映画の中では別のものになるはずでしょう。ただの証明写真かもしれない。だから写真は完成品ではなくて、材料だと思う。

肖像画を頼むときのことを考えると分かりやすいと思います。画家にスナップ写真を一枚渡して肖像画を頼む人は、写真の引き伸ばしが欲しいわけではありません。渡しているのは「この人を描いてください」という情報です。背景をどうするか、何を着せるか、どんな光にするかは、画家の仕事として任せている。写真は指示ではなく、材料なのです。

そこで作りを変えました。写真は、絵を描くAIに「入力」として渡します。添える指示はこういう趣旨です。この人の顔はこれ。骨格も、目も、口も、年齢の印象も変えない。ただし服と背景は写真から持ってこない。この映画の絵柄で、この映画にふさわしい格好で、描き直す。

冒頭の三枚は、その仕組みの出力です。顔は写真から。服は映画から。あの紺のTシャツが消えていたのは、機能が壊れているからではなく、機能が正しく働いているからでした。

面白いのは、この変更で、写真を上げない人も得をしたことです。前回書いたとおり、登場人物は三枚の候補から選んで確定します。確定した瞬間、その一枚が「この人の顔」として記憶される。そのあと「髪型を変えて」「服を変えて」と引き直すたびに、毎回その顔が入力として一緒に渡されます。以前は文字の説明だけで描き直していたので、服を変えるつもりが顔まで変わってしまうことがありました。いまは起きません。参考画像が人物を安定させるという、前回の選角の話と同じ原理が、ここでも効いています。

もう一つ、私がずっと気になっていた問題がありました。十二の章がある映画で、主人公が三章目で服を着替えたら、どうするのか。

答えは、服は章のものにする、でした。顔は映画全体で一つ。服は章ごとに違ってよい。この二つを別の層に分けます。

伯母の第八章で試しました。第八章は、彼女が車椅子を押して、介護してきた家族を救急外来へ運んだ日です。その日の彼女が何を着ていたか、脚本には書いてありません。でも、その章の彼女には、その章の装いがあるべきです。章を開いて「この章の服を新しく」と押すと、確定済みの顔を入力にして、服だけが違う候補が三枚出ます。一枚二セント。気に入ったものを「第八章で使う」と押せば、第八章のカットはその格好で撮られ、ほかの章はそれぞれ元のまま。第三章の服をそのまま第八章でも、というのも一回押すだけです。

結果、青いカーディガンの伯母が、麻のシャツの伯母、紺のブラウスの伯母、えんじ色のベストの伯母になりました。四枚、同じ顔。

本物の映画の現場は、考えてみれば最初からこう分かれています。俳優は俳優。役作りは役作り。衣装は衣装部が場面ごとに管理する。俳優の顔が場面ごとに変わったりはしません。私たちがやったのは、映画の現場が昔から知っている分業を、データの形でそのまま作り直しただけでした。

技術の側から言うと、この三層はこうなっています。一番下が身份——確定した顔のカード。真ん中が造型——この映画の絵柄の中でのその人の姿。一番上が服装——章ごとの装い。そしてどの服を使うかは、撮影のその瞬間に決まります。カットを一つ撮るたびに、システムは「この章のこの人は、どの装いか」を確認して、その画像を参照として映像モデルに渡す。だから章をまたいでも顔は流れず、章の中では服が揃うのです。

自分の絵を持っている人のことも考えてあります。二年間同じキャラクターを描き続けてきた作り手が、自分の設定画を持ってくる。そのとき設計のAIは、その子が誰であるかを描き直したりしません。顔は与えられたものとして受け取り、この映画の絵柄の中での姿だけを提案します。その人のキャラクターで、この現場の映画を撮る。そういう分担です。

最後に、この機能に付いている唯一の「記入欄」の話をします。写真をアップロードする前に、チェックボックスが一つあります。この画像を使う権利が自分にあること。肖像や著作権にかかわる責任は、自分が持つこと。チェックを入れないと、ファイル選択の画面は開きません。チェックした日時は、作品の記録に残ります。

この道具は「利用者は脚本以外、何も入力しない」を設計の柱にしています(その話はいずれ丸ごと一回書きます)。その道具が唯一求める入力が、文字ではなくチェック一つで、しかも内容が責任の所在だというのは、私たちなりの筋の通し方です。人は他人の写真を上げるものです。だから道具の入り口で、責任がどこにあるのかを、先に声に出して言っておく。

ちなみに、この機能を最初に試したのは私です。写真を上げたあと、次に押すボタンをしばらく探しました。どこにもありませんでした。Claudeがボタンを付け忘れていたのです。翌日には直っていました。こういう日もあります。

持ち帰るなら、この一つです。AIに何かを渡すときは、「変えてほしくないもの」と「任せるもの」を分けて渡す。写真一枚を丸ごと渡すと、AIにはTシャツまで「変えてはいけないもの」に見えてしまう。分けて渡した瞬間から、AIは材料を正しく使い始めます。

同じテーマの前回は、六セントで決めた伯母の顔の話でした。まだの方はこちらから。

text:
決定阿姨長什麼樣子，我花了六分錢。
(English version below 🇬🇧 / 日本語は下にあります 🇯🇵)

螢幕上排出三張臉。第一張，豐腴慈祥，坐在客廳裡會替你剝橘子的那種長輩。第二張，精瘦俐落，一頭銀髮剪得短短的，看得出年輕時脾氣不小。第三張，質樸，臉上有操勞的痕跡，吃藥時間要靠 AI 提醒的那種人。

先交代一下我在做什麼。我在做一個工具，把劇本變成電影。手上這份劇本，改編自我伯母的真實故事——她照顧體弱的家人很多年了，而那個家裡，有一個住在 LINE 裡的 AI：每天傳早安圖給她、教她電子琴的按鍵、連她自己的吃藥時間都記得——因為她自己也有糖尿病。第八話，是她推著輪椅、把照顧多年的家人送進急診的那一天。我想拍的，就是那一天。「阿姨」，就是劇本裡的她。

劇本裡關於她外貌的描述，只有一行：「75 歲，有糖尿病」。其他全得用推的。所以三張候選卡片底下，各有一行小字，寫它為什麼把她畫成這樣。第一張：「從糖尿病常見的體態推的」。第二張：「從她笑問 AI『是不是偷來的』那句口氣推的」。第三張：「從提醒她吃藥的場景推的」。

第二張根據的那句話，劇本裡真的有——她虧 AI 的那句「是不是偷來的」。誇獎之前，先虧一句。我喜歡她這種嘴硬。

我選了第二張。看到的瞬間就覺得，是她。會反過來虧 AI 的人，就該長這樣。

到這裡，一共六分錢。影片一秒都還沒拍。

為什麼要在開拍之前特地擋一關？說出來你可能不信：這一關，第一版根本沒有。今天就講它是怎麼來的。

第一版是我搭檔 Claude 做的。它讀完劇本，就直接去拍。一條直線，跑起來非常漂亮：劇本進去，影片出來，中間不需要我做任何事。做工具的人多半迷戀這種全自動，我承認那個畫面確實好看。

但我看著那個畫面，心裡想的是另一件事：錢。

影片十秒一塊美金，一章拍完大約二十塊。要是拍完我才發現，阿姨長得完全是另一個人，那二十塊就沒了。

而且「像不像」這件事，AI 沒辦法替我判斷。三張卡它都能畫得很好，但「哪一張是她」這個問題，系統裡沒有任何資料能回答——答案在劇本外面，只在我腦子裡。哪些事可以交給 AI、哪些事只有我能決定，這條界線我第一次看得這麼清楚。這條線之後值得用一整篇來寫。

我不會寫程式，一行 code 都看不懂，所以「這裡該怎麼寫」我沒資格跟 Claude 爭。但順序，我爭得了。我跟它說的大概是：先給我三張人物圖，不滿意可以換，因為圖便宜；選到滿意的，才准開下一步。多擋一關。

裝潢過房子的人應該懂這個道理。設計師不會第一天就叫師傅進場打牆，會先給你看 3D 圖。圖不滿意就改圖，免費；牆打下去才說不對，錢跟工期都翻好幾倍。印喜帖也一樣，印五百張之前，印刷廠會先給你看一張打樣。這些行業幾十年前就想通的事，搬到 AI 拍片上一個字都不用改：把後悔安排在最便宜的地方發生。

這個階梯具體有多陡？在這個工具裡，人物候選圖一張兩分錢，影片十秒一塊錢，一章成品大約二十塊。從圖到鏡頭是五十倍，從圖到一章是一千倍。同一個「她真的長這樣嗎」的猶豫，放在兩分錢那階，你可以反覆換到滿意為止；放到二十塊那階，猜錯一次夠你懊惱一個晚上。

不滿意的時候怎麼換，也交代一下。可以整輪重抽——再來三張新的，六分錢；也可以帶著方向重抽，「再瘦一點」「頭髮再短一點」，它會照著調。劇本裡七個角色，全部定完臉，我總共花了不到五毛錢美金。

三張這個數字，後來我也咂摸出味道。只給我一張，我只能說要或不要；三張排在一起，我就開始比較。而比較這個動作，會逼我想清楚自己到底要的是什麼。

不過老實說，一開始這些全是直覺。省多少，我說不出來。數字是後來才有的。

關卡做好之後，我們補了一個對照實驗。同樣的鏡頭——一個對白鏡、一個夜間外景、一個單人特寫——分兩批拍：一批給模型看角色參考圖，一批不給。其他條件全部相同，差別只有這一件事。

結果：沒有參考圖，一次過關 29%；有參考圖，49%。

多二十個百分點，意思是十個鏡頭裡，一次就過的從三個變五個。折成錢：每個鏡頭預期花在重拍上的費用，從一塊八毛六降到一塊一毛七，省 37%。「預期費用」聽起來抽象，其實就是保險公司算保費那一套：把「大概要重拍幾次」的機率，折算成一個價錢。而買下這整段差距的成本，是一輪選角的六分錢。

二十分，兩分錢一張的圖買到的。這是整個專案裡我最喜歡的數字。

換算到章的單位，它就不是零錢了。一章十二個鏡頭，兩邊差出來大約八塊美金——夠再多拍八十秒的片。

為什麼差這麼多？我的理解是：不給它一張臉，模型每個鏡頭都得重新想像這個人。今天想像的跟明天想像的對不上，鏡頭跟鏡頭接不起來，重拍就來了。給它一張臉，它的工作就從「創造一個人」變成「畫同一個人」。後面這件事，簡單得多。

數字出來之後，這一關的地位跟著變了：從「最好先選角」，變成「沒選角就不能拍」。

鏡頭裡會出現的角色，只要有一個臉沒定，生成鍵就按不動。我想放慢講一下這個「按不動」是怎麼做的。畫面上，它看起來只是變灰。實際上，按下去之後，後面根本沒有一條路通到生成器。Claude 沒有掛一塊「請先選角」的告示牌，它直接把那條路拆了。

告示牌要靠每個人每次都記得。家裡用電也有兩種保護法：貼一張「請勿超載」的標語，或者裝一顆保險絲。保險絲不依賴任何人的記憶。後來我發現，這個工具裡所有真正要緊的規則，Claude 全做成了保險絲，一張標語都沒有。

同一套反射，後來長遍了整個工具。比如台詞，在花任何一分錢之前，就先過一輪內容檢查——問題在修改還免費的階段就浮出來。同一顆保險絲，裝在不同的插座上。

而定好的臉，是會一路跟著走的。每拍一鏡之前，系統會確認「這一章的她是哪個造型」，把那張圖交給影片模型當參考。在關卡上鎖一次，之後每一鏡自動帶著。順帶一提，第八章的她有那一章自己的裝束——同一張臉，換上那一天的衣服。那是之後某一篇的故事。

這一關還順手定下另一件事，是關於誠實的。

前面說過，劇本裡她的外貌只有一行，其他全是推的。七個角色裡，大多數連那一行都沒有。所以立了一條規矩：推出來的臉，卡片上一定寫「從哪裡推的」。那行小字是我堅持要留的。「劇本寫的」跟「系統猜的」是兩種不同的聲明，用工具的人有權知道自己看的是哪一種。平常我們用 AI，它端出來的東西一臉篤定，哪些有根據、哪些是它自己補的，常常分不出來。至少在自己的工具裡，我想把這條線畫清楚。

還有一個細節，是很後來才補上的，但精神一樣。工具後來有了「重來」功能，整個專案可以倒回去重排。倒回去的時候，大部分東西都會重算，唯獨選角的候選圖，特地不刪：鎖解開，付過錢的圖全留在庫裡。因為其中一張，可能還是對的。

阿姨的第三張候選，那張質樸、有操勞痕跡的臉，我到現在還記得。我沒有選她。但看到那張卡的時候我就知道，這個工具真的把劇本讀進去了——「吃藥時間要靠 AI 提醒的人」，劇本裡確實有她的影子。

只是我心裡的阿姨，是會反過來虧 AI 的那一個。

如果這篇只帶走一件事，帶方法就好，它跟這個工具無關：用 AI 做任何東西，先花小錢，把「不能變的東西」鎖住——臉、商品、logo 都一樣；再花大錢生成。要猶豫，在便宜的那階猶豫；要決定，也在那階決定。

🇬🇧 English

Deciding what my aunt looks like cost me six cents.

Three faces came up on screen. The first: soft, rounded, gentle — the kind of elder who peels an orange for you in the living room. The second: lean and brisk, silver hair cropped short, a face that says she had a temper when she was young. The third: plain, years of work written into her face, the kind of person who needs an AI to remind her when to take her pills.

First, what this is. I'm building a tool that turns a screenplay into a film. The screenplay in my hands is adapted from my aunt's real life. For many years she has been the caregiver for a frail member of the family. And in that home there's an AI living inside her messaging app — it sends her a good-morning picture every day, taught her which buttons to press on her electric keyboard, and remembers her own medicine times, because she is diabetic herself. Chapter eight is the day she pushed a wheelchair and got the person she has cared for all these years to the emergency room. That's the day I wanted to film. "The aunt" is her, in the script.

The script's entire physical description of her is one line: "75, diabetic." Everything else has to be inferred. So under each candidate card there's a small line explaining why this face. The first: "from the build that often comes with diabetes." The second: "from the way she teases the AI — 'did you steal that?'" The third: "from the scenes where she's reminded to take her medicine."

The line behind that second card really is in the script: teasing the AI — "did you steal that?" A tease before any compliment. I love that stubborn streak of hers.

I picked the second. I looked at it and thought: that's her. Someone who teases her AI back should have this face.

Six cents so far. Not one second of video shot.

Why put a gate in front of the camera at all? Here's the part you may not believe: the first version didn't have one. Today's post is about how it came to exist.

The first version was built by my partner, Claude. It read the script and went straight to shooting. One straight line, and it looked beautiful running: screenplay in, footage out, nothing for me to do in between. People who build tools tend to fall in love with that kind of full automation. I'll admit the sight was impressive.

But what I was thinking about, watching it, was money.

Video costs a dollar per ten seconds. A finished chapter runs about twenty dollars. If I only found out after the shoot that the aunt had come out a complete stranger, that twenty dollars would be gone.

And "does she look right" is the one call the AI cannot make for me. It can paint all three cards beautifully. But nothing anywhere in the system can answer which one is her. The answer lives outside the script, in my head only. That's where I first saw the line between what an AI can be handed and what only I can decide — a line that deserves a whole post of its own, later.

I can't write code — can't read a line of it — so I have no standing to argue about how anything should be implemented. But I can argue about order. What I told Claude was roughly this: show me three portraits first. Let me swap them if I don't like them, because images are cheap. Only after I've settled on one should the next step open. Add a gate.

Anyone who has renovated a home knows this logic. The designer doesn't send workers in to knock down a wall on day one; they show you a 3D rendering first. Don't like the drawing? Change the drawing — it's free. Knock the wall down first and then change your mind, and the cost multiplies. Wedding invitations, same thing: before printing five hundred, the shop shows you one proof. Industries worked this out decades ago, and it transfers to AI filmmaking without changing a word: arrange for the regret to happen where it's cheapest.

How steep is the ladder, concretely? In this tool, a candidate portrait is two cents. Video is a dollar per ten seconds. A finished chapter is about twenty dollars. Portrait to shot is fifty times; portrait to chapter, a thousand. The same hesitation — is this really her face? — can be indulged as many times as you like on the two-cent rung. Guess wrong on the twenty-dollar rung and it ruins your evening.

A word on how swapping works. You can reroll a whole round — three new faces, six cents — or reroll with a direction, "thinner," "shorter hair," and it adjusts. The script has seven characters. Casting all of them cost me less than fifty cents total.

The number three turned out to matter too. Show me one face and all I can say is yes or no. Show me three and I start comparing — and comparing forces me to work out what I'm actually looking for.

Honestly, though, at the start this was all instinct. I couldn't have told you how much it saved. The numbers came later.

Once the gate existed, we ran a controlled comparison. The same shots — a dialogue shot, a night exterior, a single-character close-up — shot in two batches: one with a character reference image handed to the model, one without. Everything else identical.

The result: without the reference, 29 percent passed on the first try. With it, 49 percent.

Twenty points means that out of ten shots, first-try passes go from three to five. In money: the expected reshoot cost per shot drops from a dollar eighty-six to a dollar seventeen — 37 percent less. "Expected cost" sounds abstract, but it's the insurance company's arithmetic: take the odds of how many retakes you're likely to need and convert them into one price. And the price of buying that entire improvement was one round of casting. Six cents.

Twenty points, bought with two-cent pictures. It's my favorite number in the whole project.

Scale it to the chapter and it stops being pocket change: a chapter is twelve shots, so the gap works out to about eight dollars per chapter — enough to shoot another eighty seconds of film.

Why such a big difference? My understanding: without a face, the model has to re-imagine this person for every shot. Today's imagination doesn't match tomorrow's, shots stop matching each other, and the retakes begin. Hand it a face and the job changes from inventing a person to drawing the same person again. The second job is much easier.

Once the number existed, the gate's status changed — from "you should probably cast first" to "no casting, no camera."

If even one character in a shot has no approved face, the generate button won't fire. And I want to slow down on how it won't fire. On screen, it just looks greyed out. Underneath, pressing it leads nowhere — there is no path from that button to the generator. Claude didn't hang up a sign saying "please cast first." He removed the road.

A sign requires everyone to remember, every time. It's like electricity at home: you can tape up a note that says "don't overload this outlet," or you can install a breaker. The breaker relies on nobody's memory. I noticed later that every rule in this tool that actually matters is built as a breaker. There isn't a single sign.

The same reflex spread through the rest of the tool. Dialogue, for instance, is screened against content rules before a single cent is spent — problems surface while fixing them is still free. Same breaker, different socket.

And a locked face travels. Before each shot is generated, the system checks which look this character wears in this chapter and hands that image to the video model as the reference. Locked once at the gate, carried automatically ever after. Chapter eight, by the way, has an outfit of its own for her — same face, dressed for that day. That's a story for another post.

The gate also settled something that has nothing to do with money. It's about honesty.

As I said, the script gives her one line of appearance, and everything else is inference. Most of the seven characters don't even get the one line. So the rule is: every inferred face must say what it was inferred from. That small line under each card is one I decided to keep. "It's in the script" and "the system guessed" are two different claims, and whoever uses this tool has the right to know which one they're looking at. Most of the time, when an AI hands us something with total confidence, we can't tell how much is grounded and how much is fill. Inside my own tool, at least, I wanted that line drawn clearly.

One more detail, added much later, in the same spirit. The tool eventually got a rewind: you can roll a whole project back and start over. Rolling back regenerates most things — but the casting candidates are deliberately spared. The locks release; every image you paid for stays in the library. Because one of them might still be the right one.

I still remember my aunt's third candidate — the plain face with the years of work in it. I didn't choose her. But the moment I saw that card, I knew the tool had genuinely read the script: the person who needs the AI to remind her about her medicine really is in there somewhere.

It's just that the aunt in my head is the one who teases the AI back.

If you take one thing from this post, take the method — it isn't specific to this tool. When you make anything with AI, spend small money first to lock down whatever must not change: a face, a product, a logo. Then spend the big money to generate. Hesitate on the cheap rung. Decide on the cheap rung.

Last time I wrote about why this film exists at all. If you missed it, it's here.
https://t.co/zuWO2lFr89

🇯🇵 日本語

伯母の顔を決めるのに、私は六セント使いました。

画面に三枚の顔が並びました。一枚目は、ふくよかで穏やかな、居間でみかんを剥いてくれそうな年配の女性。二枚目は、痩せていてきびきびした、銀髪を短く切った、若い頃は気が強かっただろうという顔。三枚目は、素朴で、顔に苦労の跡があって、薬の時間をAIに教えてもらっているような人。

まず、何をしているのかを説明します。私は脚本を映画にする道具を作っています。手元の脚本は、私の伯母の実話をもとにしたものです。伯母は長年、体の弱い家族を介護してきた人です。そしてその家には、LINEの中に住むAIがいます。毎朝おはよう画像を送ってきて、電子キーボードの押し方を教えてくれて、彼女自身の薬の時間まで覚えている——伯母自身も糖尿病だからです。第八話は、彼女が車椅子を押して、介護してきた家族を救急外来へ運んだ日の話。私はその一日を、映画にしたいと思いました。「伯母」は、脚本の中の彼女のことです。

脚本にある彼女の外見の記述は、たった一行。「75歳、糖尿病」。あとは全部、推測するしかありません。だから三枚の候補カードの下には、それぞれ小さな一行が付いています。なぜこの顔にしたのか。一枚目は「糖尿病でよくある体型から」。二枚目は「AIに『それ盗んだの?』と冗談を言う口ぶりから」。三枚目は「薬の時間を教えてもらう場面から」。

二枚目の根拠になった台詞は、脚本に本当にあります。AIをからかう、あの「それ、盗んだの?」。褒める前に、まず一言からかう。私は彼女のその強がりが好きです。

私は二枚目を選びました。見た瞬間に、あの人だ、と思ったからです。AIを逆にからかう人は、この顔のはずです。

ここまでで六セント。映像はまだ一秒も撮っていません。

なぜ撮影の前に、わざわざこの関門を挟むのか。実は、最初の版にこの関門はありませんでした。今日は、それがどうやって生まれたかの話です。

最初の版は、相棒のClaudeが作りました。脚本を読み終えると、そのまま撮影に行く作りでした。一本道で、動いている姿はとてもきれいでした。脚本が入って、映像が出てくる。途中で私がすることは何もない。道具を作る側は、この「全自動」に憧れがちです。あの画面が格好いいことは認めます。

でも私がその画面を見ながら考えていたのは、別のことでした。お金です。

映像は10秒で1ドル。一章撮り終えると20ドルくらい。撮り終えてから「伯母が全然違う人だった」と気づいたら、その20ドルは消えます。

しかも「似ているかどうか」は、AIには判断できません。三枚とも上手に描くことはできる。でも「どれが彼女か」という問いに答えられる材料は、システムのどこにもない。答えは脚本の外、私の頭の中にしかないからです。AIに任せられることと、私にしか決められないことの境目が、ここに一本はっきり通っていました。この境目の話は、いずれ一回分まるごと使って書きます。

私はプログラムが書けません。コードは一行も読めない。だから「ここはこう実装するべきだ」という議論はできません。でも、順番の議論ならできます。Claudeに言ったのは、だいたいこういうことです。先に人物の絵を三枚出してほしい。気に入らなければ替えられるようにしてほしい。絵は安いから。気に入ったものが決まってから、次に進めるようにしてほしい。関門を一つ増やしてほしい。

家のリフォームをしたことがある方なら、この理屈をご存じのはずです。設計士は初日に職人を入れて壁を壊したりしません。先に3Dパースを見せてくれます。図が気に入らなければ、図を直す。無料です。壁を壊してから「違う」と言えば、お金も工期も何倍にもなる。結婚式の招待状も同じで、五百枚刷る前に、印刷屋は一枚だけ試し刷りを見せてくれます。どの業界も何十年も前に分かっていたことで、AIで映画を作る場合も一字も変えずに当てはまりました。後悔は、一番安い場所で起こす。

この階段は具体的にどれくらい急なのか。この道具では、人物の候補画像が一枚2セント。映像が10秒1ドル。一章の完成品が約20ドル。画像からカットで50倍、画像から一章なら1000倍です。同じ「本当にこの顔でいいのか」という迷いでも、2セントの段なら、納得するまで何度でもやり直せます。20ドルの段で間違えたら、一晩へこみます。

気に入らないときの替え方も書いておきます。丸ごともう一巡、新しい三枚を出し直してもらうこともできるし(六セント)、「もう少し痩せて」「髪をもっと短く」と方向を付けて出し直してもらうこともできます。脚本の登場人物は七人。全員の顔を決め終えて、合計は50セント足らずでした。

三枚という枚数にも、後から意味を感じるようになりました。一枚だけ見せられたら、言えるのは「はい」か「いいえ」だけです。三枚並ぶと、比べ始める。そして比べるという行為は、自分が何を求めているのかを考えざるを得なくさせます。

ただ、正直に言うと、最初は全部直感でした。いくら節約になるのかは言えなかった。数字が出たのは、後です。

関門ができてから、対照実験をしました。同じカット——台詞のあるカット、夜の屋外、一人の寄り——を二組に分けて撮ります。片方はモデルに人物の参照画像を渡し、片方は渡さない。条件の違いはそれだけです。

結果。参照画像なしで一発合格が29パーセント。ありで49パーセント。

20ポイントの差というのは、10カットのうち一発で通る本数が3本から5本に増えるということです。お金に直すと、1カットあたりの撮り直しの見込み費用が、1ドル86セントから1ドル17セントに下がる。37パーセントの節約です。「見込み費用」という言葉は抽象的に聞こえますが、保険会社が保険料を決めるのと同じ計算です。「何回撮り直すことになりそうか」という確率を、一つの値段に換算する。そしてこの差をまるごと買った値段が、選角一巡分の六セントでした。

20ポイントが、一枚2セントの絵で買えた。このプロジェクトで私が一番好きな数字です。

章の単位に直すと、小銭ではなくなります。一章は12カット。差は一章あたり8ドルあまり——あと80秒ぶんの映像が撮れる金額です。

なぜこんなに差が出るのか。私の理解はこうです。顔を渡さなければ、モデルは毎カット、この人物を想像し直すことになります。今日の想像と明日の想像は一致しない。カット同士がつながらない。撮り直しが発生する。顔を渡せば、仕事は「人物を創作する」から「同じ人を描く」に変わります。後者のほうが、ずっと簡単です。

数字が出てから、この関門の立場が変わりました。「できれば先に選角」から、「選角しないと撮れない」へ。

カットに登場する人物のうち一人でも顔が決まっていないと、生成ボタンは動きません。この「動かない」の作り方を、少し丁寧に書かせてください。画面の上では、ボタンは灰色になっているだけに見えます。でも実際は、押しても、その先に生成器へつながる道が存在しません。Claudeは「先に選角してください」という札を掛ける代わりに、道そのものを外しました。

札は、全員が毎回覚えていることを要求します。家の電気と同じです。「タコ足配線注意」という貼り紙を貼ることもできるし、ブレーカーを付けることもできる。ブレーカーは、誰の記憶にも頼りません。後で気づいたのですが、この道具の本当に大事なルールは、全部ブレーカーとして作られていました。貼り紙は一枚もありません。

同じ反射は、道具の他の場所にも広がっていきました。たとえば台詞は、一セントも使う前に内容チェックを通します。問題は、直すのがまだ無料の段階で浮かび上がる。同じブレーカーを、別のコンセントに付けただけです。

そして、決まった顔はその後ずっと付いて回ります。一カット撮るたびに、システムは「この章の彼女はどの装いか」を確認して、その画像を参照として映像モデルに渡す。関門で一度ロックすれば、あとは全カット自動です。ちなみに第八話の彼女には、その日のための装いがあります。同じ顔のまま、服だけその章のものに替わる。それはまた別の回の話。

この関門は、お金とは関係のないことも一つ決めました。誠実さの話です。

前に書いたとおり、脚本にある彼女の外見は一行だけで、あとは全部推測です。七人の登場人物のほとんどは、その一行すらありません。だからルールを決めました。推測した顔には、必ず「何から推測したか」を書く。あの小さな一行は、私が残すと決めたものです。「脚本に書いてある」と「システムが推測した」は別の主張で、使う側にはどちらを見ているのかを知る権利がある。普段AIを使っていて、自信満々に出てきたもののうち、どこまでが根拠のある話で、どこからが補完なのか、私たちには見分けられないことが多い。せめて自分の道具の中では、その線をはっきり引きたかった。

もう一つ、ずっと後に付いた機能ですが、同じ精神の細部があります。この道具には「やり直し」があって、プロジェクト全体を巻き戻せます。巻き戻すとほとんどのものは作り直しになりますが、選角の候補画像だけは、わざと消しません。ロックが外れるだけで、お金を払った絵は全部ライブラリに残ります。その中の一枚が、まだ正解かもしれないからです。

伯母の三枚目の候補、あの素朴で苦労の跡のある顔を、今でも覚えています。選びませんでした。でもあのカードを見たとき、この道具は本当に脚本を読んでいるのだと分かりました。「薬の時間をAIに教えてもらう人」は、確かに脚本のどこかにいます。

ただ、私の頭の中の伯母は、AIを逆にからかうほうの人でした。

この回から一つだけ持ち帰るなら、方法を持ち帰ってください。この道具に限らず使えます。AIで何かを作るとき、先に小さいお金で「変わってはいけないもの」を固定する。顔でも、商品でも、ロゴでも同じです。それから大きいお金で本番を生成する。迷うのは安い段で。決めるのも安い段で。

前回は、この映画がなぜ生まれたかを書きました。まだの方はこちらから。

True ..
Eric got recruited by Tesla Giga Nevada (LFP) in December 2024 for his strong construction and drywall background. He was a high-output Drywall & Paint Technician — fast, reliable, trained people, and made scopes run smoother.
In August 2025 he injured his left elbow (tennis elbow from repetitive drywall work). Zurich (the insurance company) denied the claim at first. He fought it, won at the hearing level, and the claim was accepted. Zurich appealed and dragged things out.
While dealing with the injury and restrictions, the workplace turned hostile. He got ridiculed, put under constant pressure, and was eventually fired in February 2026 for “attendance” even though the absences were tied to the accepted injury. He believes it was retaliation. The firing left him with financial problems (late rent, near-eviction), lost tools, and a lot of stress. His girlfriend and roommate both still work at Tesla, which made living there even harder.
Zurich finally offered a $6,000 settlement. The check was issued in June 2026. He’s been dealing with the emotional and practical fallout ever since — job hunting, considering wrongful termination options, and just trying to get back on his feet.

text:
Podcast Summary | Huberman Lab: How to Accelerate Learning & Improve Education | Joe Liemandt

Overview

Education has reached a breaking point. For over a century, the universal K-12 model has delivered access to schooling, but not universal learning. Joe Liemandt argues that the system is failing because it prioritizes grade-level content over individual mastery, allowing knowledge gaps to compound until students stall entirely. The median American student shows almost no academic progress from 8th to 12th grade. Liemandt, principal of Alpha School, presents a radical alternative: AI-powered, adaptive learning that meets students at their actual level, accelerates them 5 to 10 times faster than traditional methods, and pairs rigorous academics with entrepreneurship and life skills. His core thesis is that high standards and high support, not lowered expectations, are the key to both student happiness and achievement. The technology to overhaul education exists now, and the next 5 to 10 years will likely see a fundamental transformation of schooling.

Key Themes

- Universal access to education is not the same as universal learning. The 100-year-old Prussian model delivered schooling, but the goal of ensuring every child masters material remains unmet.

- AI is the first technology in a century capable of overhauling education. Adaptive systems that meet a student at their actual mastery level can accelerate learning 5 to 10 times faster than traditional classroom pacing.

- Knowledge gaps compound. Accepting a B-grade or 80% standard means students advance without foundational skills, making later subjects like algebra and chemistry progressively harder. Mastery at each stage is required.

- High standards and high support are the correct balance. Parents typically lean toward either high standards with low support or low standards with high support, but the effective model is both, guided by a caring adult.

- Motivation is 90% of the problem or the solution. Students need a tractable path that shows them exactly how far behind they are and how quickly they can catch up, rather than a vague "3 years behind."

- Schools should be measured by growth rate, not starting achievement level. A school's job is to accelerate development regardless of a child's starting point, so the slope of the learning line matters more than the absolute level.

- The human element is irreplaceable. AI will not replace teachers because the core function is convincing a student they are capable of more, which is a relational act.

- Real support means individualized instruction with mastery, not platitudes like "do your best" that avoid both standards and actual help. This is how sports coaching operates, and academics should follow the same model.

Detailed Summary

The current education system was built over a hundred years ago in Prussia, pulling kids off farms into classrooms with a teacher at the front. This model persists universally across rich and poor schools, delivering universal access but not universal learning. Liemandt argues that academic standards have been pulled away over time, and knowledge gaps compound. A student who scores 710 on the math SAT but makes "careless errors" is often actually struggling with un-mastered third-grade multiplication tables. Once those facts are memorized, the score can jump to 790. A student's working memory has a limited number of slots; if calculations consume those slots, there is no room left for the actual problem. The issue is not the algebra, it is the third grade math facts. A student entering chemistry needs algebra, which requires fraction fluency, which depends on memorized multiplication tables. Accepting a B and moving on ensures these gaps persist.

The consequences are stark. On the NWEA MAP test, the average 8th grader advances only about one point by 12th grade, from 233 to 234 on a 300-point scale. This implies essentially no learning in four years for the median student. Students arriving at Alpha School from elite $50,000 private schools were on average 2.2 grade levels behind on entrance assessments, revealing systemic failure even in top-tier institutions. The shame of being behind is a major barrier, often rooted in childhood trauma like a dyslexic student being laughed at for writing a 7 backwards. An AI tutor offers a private, judgment-free space to work below grade level and close gaps without peers observing.

The solution is AI-driven adaptive learning. Effective AI education is not a chatbot, because most kids would use it to cheat. It is an adaptive system that assesses a student's precise gaps, delivers lessons at their actual mastery level, and requires repetition to fluency. The data supports the model. Alpha students spend an average of 121 minutes per day on the AI app and learn more than twice what they would in six hours of class plus homework. This yields 5 to 10 times normal learning speed, allowing a student who is three years behind to catch up in about 90 days at one hour per day. The app uses worked examples, where a solved problem is shown and scaffolding is progressively removed, followed by spaced repetition that reminds the user right before forgetting to transfer knowledge to long-term memory.

The pedagogy is grounded in cognitive science, which is largely absent from teacher training. At a staff day, only 5% of teachers knew what direct instruction was, and none knew Project Follow Through, the largest educational study on effective teaching from the 1970s. Unlike neuroscience or biochemistry, education lacks a fact-based canon and standardized textbooks. This leads to a "religious war" between inquiry learning and direct instruction. There is also an empirical question of whether initial mastery, drilling to 95%+ correct at first exposure, is necessary. Alpha's data shows that worked examples plus spaced repetition outperformed in grades 8-12 for complex algebra problems but underperformed in grades 4-7 for easier problems, so initial mastery was re-added for younger grades.

Motivation is the critical lever. The goal is to shift a student's self-perception from "I can do hard things" to "I can do what I thought were hard things." Suffering is only productive when tied to purpose; forcing struggle without buy-in is ineffective. This means making learning doable by delivering material at the right level, then gating desired activities behind academic completion. The sports academy model demonstrates this. Over 1000 middle and high school students, academically years behind, learn two times in two hours by being given lessons at their actual level, like third-grade material for an 8th grader, making the work doable. At noon, if the AI confirms they are on track, they get to play basketball. Academics are gated to access sports, and college coaches reportedly prefer equivalent athletes who have done hard things academically, doubling the odds of a D1 scholarship. Alpha also uses aggressive motivators, including paying kids cash for top scores. Public schools cannot legally do this, which is a barrier that should be changed.

The school environment is deliberately different. Alpha students spend only two hours per day on core academics, with no gaps, and the rest of the day on entrepreneurship, financial literacy, and communication skills. Kindergarteners learn to earn, save, spend, invest, and donate. Middle schoolers run Airbnbs, launch food trucks, and manage vending machines, learning gross margin. The curriculum starts with five stacks in kindergarten: leadership and teamwork, entrepreneurship and financial literacy, socialization and relationship building, storytelling and public speaking, and grit and hard work. Milestones scale up, from 5K runs in second grade to a team-based tough mudder in eighth grade. Ninety percent of Alpha students say they love school, and 40 to 60% say they would rather go to school than vacation. Eighty-five percent of parents saw their child do something they thought impossible for their age, like kindergarteners climbing a 40-foot rock wall or riding bikes five miles across the Golden Gate Bridge.

The model prioritizes life skills and purpose. The new Founder School high school program promises each student will earn $1 million in profit from a business or get tuition back. It is designed for "philosopher builders," where kids willingly accept hard academics because they are tied to entrepreneurial goals. Examples include a student who produced a Broadway musical in 1,000-person venues using TikTok-sourced music and another who became the first high school lead researcher published in Nature, training an LLM to give teens social-emotional advice. The school's three commitments are love school more than vacation, progress at twice the rate in two hours, and learn all the life skills you want. Liemandt's personal story illustrates the importance of purpose: he was a minimum-effort student in high school and Stanford, dropped out, and only then did his father see his work ethic through his 100-hour weeks. Kids will work harder when the purpose is internalized. The tension for parents in middle and high school is whether to unlock a child's potential or impose their own value system. Leaning into what the child loves leads to incredibly hard things, while pushing against their interests yields pushback. High standards are not the enemy; effective suffering comes from setting standards that align with what kids want to become. The mental health issues in elite schools stem from kids being forced into roles they do not want. The right approach is helping kids achieve their own ambitions while maintaining requirements for participation.

text:
Sadhguru’s wife, Vijayakumari (known as Vijji), died in January 1997 at the Isha Yoga Center in Tamil Nadu.

The Spiritual Account: Sadhguru and his followers state that she attained Mahasamadhi. This is a yogic process where a realized person consciously chooses to leave their physical body.

The Allegations: Months after her death, her father filed a police complaint. He suspected foul play because her body was cremated quickly and raised questions about the circumstances of her death.

Police InvestigationThe police transferred the case to the local rural police for a detailed investigation.

Investigators questioned witnesses, doctors, and people at the ashram.The police found no proof of foul play or murder and officially closed the case.

So, why was the cremation done before even Viji's father arrived. And there is one space at Isha Coimbatore where a space is dedicated to her.

If permissions are sorted, they can carbon date her mortal remains.

In Hinduism, known as Antyesti, is the traditional funeral rite intended to release a person's soul from its physical body so it can reincarnate or achieve liberation (moksha). 

The rituals usually take place quickly, often within 24 hours of death.

Preparation: Family members wash the body with holy water (often from the Ganges river) and milk.

Dressing: The body is wrapped in a shroud. Typically, white cloth is used for men and widows, while red or bright colors are used for married women.

The Pind Daan: Rice balls (pindas) and water are offered to the soul to sustain it during its transition.

The Procession: Family and friends carry the body on a simple wooden stretcher to the cremation ground (shmashana), chanting prayers like "Ram Naam Satya Hai" (The name of God is truth).

text:
Iran’s 18 Million Toman Government Salary Struggles Against Tehran Food Prices

For lower-paid government employees in Iran, a monthly salary of around 18 million toman leaves increasingly little room for basic household expenses as food prices take up a large share of earnings.

A review of grocery prices displayed on Digikala  in Tehran at approximately 8 p.m. ET on Aug. 31 shows the pressure facing workers at the lower end of the government pay scale.

The listings show that even ordinary staples can quickly eat into a monthly paycheck. Milk was priced at roughly 45,000 to 135,000 toman per bottle or carton, depending on size, brand and discounts. One 945 ml bottle of low-fat milk was listed at about 131,575 toman.

Eggs represented an even larger expense. Packages of 20 eggs were selling for roughly 502,000 to 532,000 toman, while a 30-egg package was listed at approximately 588,000 toman.

Traditional breads, including sangak, lavash, barbari and taftoon, were generally available for around 27,000 to 34,000 toman per order.

Protein costs put still more pressure on household budgets. One listing for approximately 1.8 kilograms of boneless, skinless chicken breast was 1,251,600 toman. A 500-gram package of lamb tail fat was listed at 714,000 toman.

For a government employee taking home around 18 million toman a month, the numbers add up quickly.

If that worker tried to limit groceries to 20 to 30 percent of monthly income, the entire food budget would amount to only 3.6 million to 5.4 million toman.

A single purchase of a 20-pack of eggs and 1.8 kilograms of chicken breast would cost roughly 1.75 million toman. That is nearly 10 percent of the worker’s entire monthly salary.

Those two items alone would consume about 32 percent of a 5.4 million toman grocery budget. For someone limiting food spending to 3.6 million toman, they would take up almost half of the month’s grocery money.

And that calculation does not include rice, vegetables, fruit, cooking oil, bread, additional milk and eggs, tea or other household staples. Nor does it account for rent, transportation, utilities, medicine, clothing and other expenses competing for the same monthly paycheck.

The prices provide a stark illustration of the purchasing power available to Iran’s lower-paid public employees. An 18 million toman monthly salary can cover basic groceries, but doing so can require sacrificing a substantial portion of income, leaving considerably less for housing and other necessities.

The Digikala figures are a snapshot of online retail prices available in Tehran on Aug. 31 and should not be interpreted as official nationwide averages. Prices differ by store, neighborhood, brand and promotions. Still, they offer a direct look at the prices Tehran consumers were encountering and the difficult arithmetic facing workers living on the lower end of government pay.

text:
Aston Villa vs Arsenal Player-by-Player Analysis 

- David Raya
Quiet afternoon. Villa generated almost nothing of quality and Raya faced no shots on target. Meanwhile, he commanded his box well, distributed cleanly under limited pressure, and helped the team see out the final 30 minutes without drama.

- Ben White
Started as expected and overlapped well with Saka as usual. Contributed to build-ups and stayed disciplined after the goal. Won his duels and was reliable as ever in a game that suited his positioning.

- Cristhian Mosquera
Started next to Gabriel again with Saliba out. Involved in the build-up to the goal (found Eze). Looked composed until he grabbed the back of his leg around the 72nd minute and had to come off allowing Konsa to make his Arsenal debut as a replacement. Solid until the injury.

- Gabriel Magalhães 
Anchored the back line. Won aerials, organized the defence after the goal, and helped Arsenal sit in a low block. Physical presence suited Villa’s direct moments. Typical performance as usual.

- Riccardo Calafiori 
Key in the goal: received a pass from Eze, drove to the byline and cut the ball back for Saka. Offered width and progressive passing from left-back. Defended his side well against Villa’s right-sided threats. One of the more influential performers.

- Ezri Konsa (sub)
Came on for the injured Mosquera against his former club to a mixed reception. Helped see the game out. Limited minutes but no obvious issues.

- Declan Rice
Sat deepest, broke up play, and recycled possession. Replaced late by Zubimendi as Arsenal looked to close the game. Typical controlling performance in a match that became attritional.

- Myles Lewis-Skelly
Started in midfield and covered a lot of ground. Progressive with the ball and helped Arsenal dominate first-half possession. Replaced around the 72nd minute by Guimarães.

- Martin Ødegaard
Dictated tempo in midfield. Involved in the build-up and kept the ball moving in tight spaces. Replaced later by Merino as Mikel freshened the midfield. Needs to do more to operate fluidly across the front line and not just be one-directional toward the Saka-Ben White angle.

- Bruno Guimarães (sub)
Came on around the 72nd minute alongside Merino. Added physicality and helped Arsenal manage the game after taking the lead. Useful cameo on his way back from injury.

- Mikel Merino (sub)
Came on with Guimarães. Helped congest midfield and protect the lead. Limited attacking involvement as the game slowed.

- Martín Zubimendi (sub)
Late replacement for Rice. Helped see out added time.

- Bukayo Saka
Match-winner. Timed his run perfectly to meet Calafiori’s cut-back and finished past Suzuki in the 59th minute; his second goal in two league games. Combined well with White and Ødegaard on the right. The difference-maker.

- Christos Tzolis
Hard a difficult game today. Involved early but picked up a yellow card and was replaced at half-time by Eze. Showed the directness that made him a strong signing, but the game became more physical than fluid.

- Kai Havertz 
Lacklustre performance if though he held the ball up well in a match with few clear chances. Worked hard without a goal this time.

- Eberechi Eze (sub)
Half-time replacement for Tzolis. Involved in the goal: received from Mosquera and slipped Calafiori in. Added energy and quality on the left after the break. Positive impact off the bench.

text:
A detail in a credit union case study from late last year explains why every corporate deepfake statistic in circulation is unreliable.

Michigan State University Federal Credit Union, $8.26 billion in assets and 367,000 members, deployed call-centre deepfake detection in August 2024. Between then and September 2025 it traced $2.57 million in avoided fraud exposure from intercepted deepfake calls, roughly a quarter of a million dollars a month.

The important sentence is not that figure. It is the explanation of why the figure had never existed before. The VP of the member service centre said the institution had no system giving full visibility into fraud exposure in the contact centre, that transactional fraud monitoring was well handled but call-channel exposure was not, and that the new tooling was what allowed them to start measuring it accurately.

So the number is a product of the deployment. Before it, this attack volume was invisible, not absent.

Now generalise. Institutions without detection in the voice channel are not reporting low deepfake incidence. They are reporting no measurement. Every survey asking whether an organization has experienced a deepfake attack is measuring detection capability as much as attack volume, and the gap between the two is unknown and probably large.

Two further points from the same case.

The deployment paid for itself twice. Passive authentication replaced manual security questions and cut 58 seconds from average authentication time per call, and the Net Promoter Score moved from 57 to 63 in the month following go-live. Security controls that reduce friction rather than adding it are rare enough to be worth noting.

And the targeting is moving downmarket. The assessment offered in the piece is that fraudsters are turning to credit unions and smaller community banks precisely because larger institutions have invested in defences that these have not.

Two caveats worth stating plainly. Avoided exposure is not the same as realised loss prevented, and the measurement comes from the vendor whose product produced it. The structural insight holds regardless.

text:
✨The BASIS of our state flag is the Regimental Banner of the 1st Minnesota Volunteer Infantry Regiment
~The farmer & the Native American on horseback, "L'Etoile du Nord" for French Voyageurs, & Mississippi River w/ Saint Anthony Falls.

✨Our state history👇
Minnesota became a state in 1858, just 3 years prior to the Civil War which broke-out in 1861.
On that day, Minnesota's first Governor, Alexander Ramsey, was in Washington DC meeting w/ Lincoln when the Confederates attacked Fort Sumter marking the beginning of the Civil War. Ramsey immediately offered 1,000 men to the Union army, making him the very first governor to do so.

The 1st Minnesota Volunteer Infantry Regiment was all-volunteer men who served 3-year commitments.

During combat actions, fighting to save the union & free the slaves, they sustained massive casualties at the Battle of Bull Run (20%), Antietam (28%), & a staggering 82% at the Battle of Gettysburg where the regiment's most famous actions occurred on the second day of the battle.

The 1st MN was outnumbered, 3 or 4 to one, by the Confederates & charged them in a suicide mission to protect the Union line & give Union reinforcements time to arrive.

The 1st MN Volunteer Infantry Regiment's 82% casualty rate still stands as the largest loss by any surviving U.S. military unit, in a single day's engagement, in United States history. 

Dates on our flag:
~1819- Fort Snelling founded
~1858- MN statehood
~1893- flag adoption (first 35 years after statehood we did not have a state flag, finally got it for 1893 Chicago World's Fair).

~19 gold stars arranged in clusters forming a 5-pointed-star symbolizing Minnesota as the 19th state admitted to the union after the original 13 states. The very top star is bigger than the others to represent the North Star.

~Wreath of pink & white Lady Slippers (Moccasins)- state flower.
~3 Norway Pines (state tree) for the 3 pine regions: St. Croix, Lake Superior, & Mississippi River.

~Saint Anthony Falls, also known as Owámniyomni, holds deep spiritual significance for the Dakota. The falls are considered a sacred site, a place of spiritual power, & connection to the natural world. The Dakota performed ceremonies & offerings at the falls, respecting its power & recognizing its life-giving properties. The Dakota associated the falls w/ legends & spirits, including Oanktehi, god of waters & evil, who lived beneath the falling water.
The falls were a natural resting & trade point along the Mississippi between Dakota & Anishinaabe/Ojibwe peoples.

The DFL Trifecta & Steve Simon erased our entire state history when they controlled our state gov't in 2023-2024.

text:
Compared to global standards, Japanese engineers' salaries were remarkably low, leading to a rise in cases where Korean or Chinese companies lured them with high pay for side gigs or full-time job switches.  

After Japan's electrical manufacturers shifted from self-made leaders—who had developed radar and sonar during the war—to salaried managers, risky, ambitious R&D took a backseat to short-term profit-boosting layoffs.  

Whenever Japanese companies laid off staff, that talent flowed overseas; when they closed factories, production equipment was sold off cheaply abroad. This cycle repeated.  

Even when major electrical manufacturers' semiconductor divisions posted huge profits, those gains were siphoned off company-wide, with no strategic reinvestment into the semiconductor units.  

Japanese semiconductor makers began losing out in mass production to bolder investors like Korean chip firms.  

If things continue on the current trajectory, Japan's appliance manufacturers are highly likely to follow the same path as America's once-dominant ones.  

Today, the bulk of SONY's sales and profits come from gaming, entertainment, movies, music, and finance.  

It's a different form from the classic appliance-maker SONY of old, but like GE, it'll survive by transforming.  

If you strip out heavy electricals, entertainment, and finance to compare pure appliance and semiconductor sales, the reality is that even all Japan's electrical giants combined can't touch Samsung alone.  

Chinese manufacturers and the like are now acquiring famous Japanese brands to slap nostalgic Japanese labels on Chinese products, making it easier for Japanese consumers to buy with confidence.  

The NEC-branded PCs on sale today? The products and the company are Lenovo. (A 100% subsidiary of Lenovo NEC Holdings B.V.)  

Fujitsu's PC arm, Fujitsu Client Computing Limited, is 51% owned by Lenovo Group Limited, giving Lenovo the reins.  

Toshiba's Dynabook brand and Sharp are now under Taiwan's Hon Hai Precision Industry (Foxconn Group).  

America's once-shining appliance giants vanished from the market as a result of Japan's appliance boom.  

In their place, the U.S. has seen the rise of so-called Big Tech: Apple, Microsoft, Google, Meta (formerly Facebook), Amazon.  

All started as garage operations with a handful of people—classic venture firms.  

Even as its appliance makers faded, America's innovative drive hasn't waned.  

Emerging companies like SpaceX and Tesla are thriving in droves.  

And these firms wield global influence.  

In Japan, too, we hope new enterprises will rise to replace declining traditional giants.  

No matter how small the company or individual, rather than pulling down those striving to achieve something, we need to rally around them—like the early days of Apple.  

To those looking to start something: I hope you'll challenge yourselves with business plans that target the vast global market, not just the limited domestic one.  

The Microcomputer Museum offers the "High-Tech Lab Project" as a hands-on learning space for promising teens in their 10s, providing foundational tech skills that'll serve them for life and help them thrive in the future.  

Tech fields are like art or sports: To excel as an engineer, hands-on experience starting at age 10 is key.  

The High-Tech Lab Project awaits your support and the participation of promising teens in their 10s.

text:
歴史は繰り返します。
かつてアメリカには、巨大家電メーカーが君臨していました。

RCA社:(カラーTV放送方式のNTSCを開発、RCAコネクタに名前が残る)

GE(General Electric)社:(トーマス・エジソンが設立した由緒ある巨大企業)

Zenith Electronics社:(アマチュア無線家が創業、米国の松下的企業、現在は韓国LGの子会社)

Magnavox社:(ボイスコイルを使ったスピーカーを発明、現在はPhilipsの子会社)

Philco社:(ラジオおよびテレビの普及期において市場をリードした先駆的メーカー)

Sylvania社:(1901年に創業されたアメリカの歴史ある大手電気・照明機器メーカー)

昭和30年代～40年代の日本の家電メーカーは束になっても、これらの米国家電メーカーの足元にも及びませんでした。

昭和30年代(1955年代)に、日本のお金持ちの家に行くと、RCA社のTV、GE社のエアコンが在りました。

日本の家電メーカーは、これらの米国家電メーカーのTV受像機等を購入して「生体解剖」と言われるリバース・エンジニアリングを行い、事実上の「パクリ」製品を製造していました。

昭和50年(1975年代)に低価格で高信頼、小さい、という特徴を持った日本製の家電製品が、米国を初めとして欧州から中東地域まで、大量に輸出されました。

この日本家電躍進の原動力となったのは、大量の安い労働力と、米国が役立たないと予想した「トランジスタ」の改良を行い、トランジスタ技術を米国より早く実用化した事でした。(米国企業は、トランジスタでは、信頼性の確保、高周波、高電圧、大電流の制御は難しいと予想した)

日本の家電メーカーの躍進により、米国の全ての家電メーカーは、撤退、倒産、買収により市場から消えました。

日本の家電メーカーが、米国の家電メーカーのブランドを購入して、米国民が安心して購入できる歴史ある米国家電メーカーのブランド名で日本製品を発売した事もありました。

実例として、1980年代、NECは米国の老舗ブランド名「パッカードベル」を取得して、NECのPC製品に「パッカードベル」ブランドを標示して、米国製品風の雰囲気を出して、米国民が安心して購入できるように販売していました。

表示写真は、「パッカードベル」(Packard Bell)ブランドを標示するNECの米国事務所。

その頃、歴史の繰り返しが始まりかけていました。

1980年頃、NECの技術者は、「三星(現:サムスン)は、ケーブル作りの下請けとして使っている。製造技術がまだまだなので、NECの技術者が現地に出向いて、製造技術を指導している」と館長に語っていました。

1986年頃に館長は、Z80を搭載した少し複雑なCPU基板の製造を、三星(現:サムスン)と、ラッキーゴールドスター(現:LG)へ、正式ルートを使い、各社の上層部へ依頼しました。

その時の回答は、「現時点では、依頼いたいた基板を我々は製造出来ない。しかし、将来、この基板を作れるようなるため、我々は努力を続ける」という回答が館長にありました。

現在、世界的なハイテクブランドとして躍進している「サムスン」と「LG」の1986年頃の技術力は、少し複雑なZ80 CPU基板を製造できないレベルだった事に注目してください。

1990年頃、毎週日曜の夜に、成田空港の入国ロビーの出口にビデオカメラを設置して、入国者の撮影行為が行われている、という話題が広がりました。

日本人技術者が、週末を利用して、韓国企業で技術指導のアルバイトをしている例が増えて、その証拠集めで、日本企業側が日曜の夜に韓国から帰国する人達を撮影していたとの事でした。

1990年代前半ぐらいに、SONYの社内で衝撃的なレポートが回覧されました。

サムスン社の家庭用TVの性能が、SONYの家庭用ローエンドTV製品の性能を上回ったという内容でした。(噂では無く、SONYの技術職から館長が直接聴いた話)

日本の技術者の給与水準が世界レベルと比較して、とても低いので、日本の技術者へ、韓国企業や中国企業が高給でアルバイトや、転職するよう誘う事例が増えました。

日本の電機メーカーの経営者が、戦争中にレーダーやソナーを開発していた、たたき上げ技術者の出身者から、サラリーマン経営者に世代交代してからは、リスクが有る挑戦的な開発事業より、短期的に利益が上がるリストラが優先されました。

日本企業がリストラすると、リストラされた人材が海外に流失して、日本企業が工場を閉鎖すると、生産設備が安価で海外に売却されるという繰り返しになりました。

大手電機メーカーの半導体部門が高利益を上げても、その利益は、全社的に利用されて、半導体部門への戦略的投資には使われませんでした。

大胆な戦略投資を行う、韓国などの半導体メーカーに、日本の半導体メーカーが量産規模で負けるようになりました。

現在のベクトルのまま進行すると、日本の家電メーカーは、かつての米国の家電メーカーと同じ道を進む可能性が高いです。

現在のSONYの売り上げと利益の大部分は、ゲーム、エンタメ、映画、音楽、金融です。

かつての家電メーカーだった頃のSONYとは別の形態ですが、GEと同じで、形を変えて生き残るでしょう。

重電やエンタメ、金融などを除く、純粋な家電や半導体の売り上げを比較すれば、日本の電機メーカーが束になってもサムスン社1社に及ばないほどの差が付いているのが現実です。

中国メーカーなどは、日本人が安心して中国製品を購入するように、日本の有名ブランドを取得して、中国製品に日本の懐かしいブランドを付けて売るようになっています。

今売られているNECブランドのパソコンは、製品も会社もレノボです。(Lenovo NEC Holdings B.Vの100％子会社)

富士通のPC会社である富士通クライアントコンピューティング株式会社は、Lenovo Group Limited が51%の株式を所有して、レノボが主導権を持っています。

TOSHIBAのダイナブックブランドとシャープは、台湾の鴻海精密工業(フォックスコングループ)傘下になっています。

かつて輝いていた米国の家電メーカーは、日本の家電メーカーの大躍進の結果、市場から消えました。

その代わり、米国では、ビックテックと呼ばれる、Apple、Microsoft、Google、Meta(旧Facebook)、Amazonが成長しています。

いずれも、ガレージから少人数で創業したベンチャー企業です。

米国の家電メーカーが消えても、米国の成長力は衰えていません。

スペースX社、テスラ社を初めとする新興企業も多数活躍しています。

そして、これらの企業は、世界的な影響力を持っています。

日本でも、衰退する伝統的大企業に代わる、新しい企業が育つ事が望まれます。

どんなに小さい規模の会社や個人でも、何かを成し遂げようとする方の足を引っ張るのではなく、創業時のApple社のように、みんなで応援する行動が必要と思います。

何かを始めようという方は、国内の限定されたマーケットではなく、巨大な世界マーケットを狙えるビジネスプランに挑戦される事を願います。

マイコン博物館 では、将来有望な10歳代の子供達が、将来、活躍できるよう、一生役立つ基礎技術の体験学習の場として「ハイテックラボ・プロジェクト」を提供しています。

技術分野は、芸術やスポーツと同じで、技術者として活躍するには10歳からの体験が重要です。

ハイテックラボ・プロジェクトでは、皆様のご支援と、将来有望な10歳代の子供達の参加をお待ちしています。

text:
The Auspicious Visit of His Holiness Shastri Shri Madhavpriyadasji Maharaj to Arsha Vidya Mandir, Vadodara

Meaningful Deliberations on Sanatana Dharma, Cow Protection, and the Spiritual Renewal of Society

His Holiness Shastri Shri Madhavpriyadasji Maharaj of SGVP Gurukul visited Arsha Vidya Mandir, Vadodara, sanctifying the ashram with his holy presence and blessings. As a deeply cherished and close friend of His Holiness Swami Shri Paramatmanandaji, his visit was filled with affection, warmth, and spiritual camaraderie.

His Holiness Shastriji Maharaj visited the Shri Omkareshwar Temple, the Annapurna Sadhu Cottages, and the goshala within the ashram premises. He was deeply impressed by the ashram’s purity, discipline, thoughtful functioning, and well-organized administration, and wholeheartedly appreciated the various service and educational activities undertaken by the ashram.

Expressing his happiness at the ashram’s continued progress and the expansion of its service activities, His Holiness Shastriji Maharaj offered his affectionate blessings to Pujya Swamini Dhanyanandaji and conveyed his best wishes for the continued growth of the ashram’s work in knowledge, spiritual practice, and service.

On this occasion, His Holiness Shastriji Maharaj and His Holiness Swami Shri Paramatmanandaji engaged in profound and meaningful discussions on important subjects, including the preservation and promotion of Sanatana Dharma and Hindu culture, the service and protection of Gau Mata, and the restoration of eternal moral and spiritual values in society.

The two revered saints also reflected on the future projects of Acharya Sabha, its broader social responsibilities, and forthcoming efforts for the welfare of society.

This sacred meeting was far more than an affectionate encounter between two saintly hearts—it became a remarkable confluence of knowledge and devotion, spiritual practice and service, tradition and vision for the future.

This shared resolve to carry the eternal light of Sanatana culture to every individual and to empower society along the path of dharma, values, and service will undoubtedly offer new inspiration and direction in the times to come.

परम पूज्य शास्त्री श्री माधवप्रियदासजी महाराज का अर्ष विद्या मंदिर, वडोदरा में पावन आगमन

सनातन धर्म, गौ-संरक्षण एवं समाज के आध्यात्मिक पुनर्जागरण पर सार्थक विमर्श
एसजीवीपी गुरुकुल के परम पूज्य शास्त्री श्री माधवप्रियदासजी महाराज ने अर्ष विद्या मंदिर, वडोदरा में पधारकर आश्रम को अपने पावन सान्निध्य एवं आशीर्वाद से अभिसिंचित किया। परम पूज्य स्वामी श्री परमात्मानंदजी के अत्यंत आत्मीय एवं प्रिय मित्र के रूप में उनका यह आगमन स्नेह, सौहार्द और आध्यात्मिक आत्मीयता से ओतप्रोत रहा।

परम पूज्य शास्त्रीजी महाराज ने आश्रम परिसर स्थित श्री ओंकारेश्वर मंदिर, अन्नपूर्णा साधु कुटियाओं एवं गोशाला का दर्शन किया। आश्रम की शुचिता, अनुशासन, सुविचारित कार्यप्रणाली एवं सुव्यवस्थित व्यवस्थापन से वे अत्यंत प्रभावित हुए और आश्रम द्वारा संचालित विविध सेवा एवं शिक्षण गतिविधियों की हृदयपूर्वक प्रशंसा की।

आश्रम की निरंतर प्रगति एवं सेवा-गतिविधियों के विस्तार पर प्रसन्नता व्यक्त करते हुए परम पूज्य शास्त्रीजी महाराज नेआश्रम के ज्ञान, साधना और सेवा के कार्यों के उत्तरोत्तर विस्तार की मंगलकामना की।
इस अवसर पर परम पूज्य शास्त्रीजी महाराज एवं परम पूज्य स्वामी श्री परमात्मानंदजी के मध्य सनातन धर्म एवं हिंदू संस्कृति के संरक्षण-संवर्धन, गौ माता की सेवा एवं संरक्षण तथा समाज में शाश्वत नैतिक एवं आध्यात्मिक मूल्यों की पुनर्स्थापना जैसे महत्वपूर्ण विषयों पर गहन एवं सार्थक विचार-विमर्श हुआ।

दोनों संतों ने आचार्य सभा के भावी प्रकल्पों, व्यापक सामाजिक दायित्वों एवं लोककल्याण की दिशा में किए जाने वाले आगामी प्रयासों पर भी मनन किया।

Family of murdered Coast Guard pilot raises reward to $30K

The family of a U.S. Coast Guard rescue pilot who was killed in a random shooting in Skyway is pleading for answers, now offering a $30,000 reward for information that leads to his killer.

The family of Coast Guard Lt. Connor Overstreet is offering a $30,000 reward for information leading to an arrest in his Skyway killing.
